s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Bend Over, Straighten Up
s.d: to bend over and stoop down, with perhaps greater emphasis on the position being ‘down’ than in the case of {L:κύπτω<SDBG:κύπτω:000000>} ({D:17.29})
s.g: to bend down; to bend over; to stoop down

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Bend Over, Straighten Up
s.d: to bend over into a stooping position
s.g: to bend down; to stoop down

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: (derivative of {L:κράτος<SDBG:κράτος:000000>}[a] ‘power,’ {D:76.6}) pertaining to being powerful or mighty
s.c: In ⟦1 Peter 5:6|1 Peter 5:6⟧ χεῖρ is, of course, to be interpreted as power (see LN 76.3).

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Health, Vigor, Strength
s.d: to become strong and healthy, with the implication of physical vigor
s.c: In employing an expression to translate ‘to become strong,’ it is important to avoid the impression of ‘to become muscular.’ The emphasis is upon total physical vigor, not mere muscular strength.

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: (derivative of {L:κραταιός<SDBG:κραταιός:000000>} ‘powerful,’ {D:76.9}) to become strong psychologically
s.g: to become strong; to become powerful
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 16:13|1 Corinthians 16:13⟧ κραταιόομαι must be understood in a non-physical sense. The implication is that the believer is to be sufficiently strong as to be able to dominate any evil influence.

s.dp: Attachment › Grasp, Hold
s.d: to hold on to an object
s.g: to hold on to; to retain in the hand; to seize

s.dp: Control, Rule › Control, Restrain
s.d: to exercise power or force over someone or something
s.g: to have power over; to control
s.c: See discussion at LN 37.17.

s.dp: Control, Rule › Seize, Take into Custody
s.d: to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cause a state to continue, on the basis of some authority or power
s.g: to hold; to keep; to cause to continue
s.c: In this expression in ⟦John 20:23|John 20:23⟧ it is the state of being guilty of sin which is caused to continue. See also discussion at LN 40.8.

s.dp: Aspect › Complete, Finish, Succeed
s.d: to be able to complete or finish, presumably despite difficulties
s.g: to accomplish; to do successfully; to carry out

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to having noble status, with the implication of power and authority, often employed as a title

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: the power to rule or control

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: a deed manifesting great power, with the implication of some supernatural force

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: to shout or cry out, with the possible implication of the unpleasant nature of the sound{N:001}

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: the sound of a loud scream or shout

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to weep or wail, with emphasis upon the noise accompanying the weeping
s.g: to weep; to wail; to lament; weeping; crying

s.dp: Foods and Condiments › Food
s.d: the flesh of animals used as food
s.c: In some languages a distinction is made between the meat of wild animals and meat of domesticated animals. In ⟦Romans 14:21|Romans 14:21⟧ and ⟦1 Corinthians 8:13|1 Corinthians 8:13⟧ it is the latter which is involved.

s.dp: Value › Good, Bad
s.d: pertaining to being superior to something else in characteristics or function

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to having a higher status in comparison to something else

s.dp: Attachment › Fasten, Stick To
s.d: to cause to hang down from
s.g: to make to hang; to be hung from

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to hang on a tree) to execute someone by nailing that person to a cross
s.c: It is possible to understand ξύλου in ⟦Acts 5:30|Acts 5:30⟧ as ξύλον ‘cross’ (LN 6.28) and to interpret the expression literally as ‘… you seized and killed by hanging him on a cross.’

s.dp: Attachment › Fasten, Stick To
s.d: to hang down from some point
s.g: to hang from; to hang down from

s.dp: Relations › Dependency
s.d: to be in a relation of dependency upon something
s.c: In a number of languages dependency as in ⟦Matthew 22:40|Matthew 22:40⟧ may be expressed as ‘to hang on’ or ‘to be tied together by’ or ‘only have meaning because of.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Elevated Land Formations
s.d: steep slope, steep side of a hill

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Κρήτη<SDBG:Κρήτη:000000>} ‘Crete,’ {D:93.508}) a person who is a native of Crete

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a companion of Paul

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island south of Greece

s.dp: Plants › Fruit Parts of Plants
s.d: a grain somewhat similar to wheat, but regarded as less desirable for food
s.c: In a number of languages there is no specific term for barley, and therefore it may be useful simply to borrow a term from a dominant language. In certain instances, however, translators have used an expression such as ‘wheat-like grain.’ It may even be useful to have a footnote to explain something of the nature of barley, but the fact that it was cheaper than wheat is clear from ⟦Revelation 6:6|Revelation 6:6⟧.

s.dp: Plants › Fruit Parts of Plants
s.d: (derivative of {L:κριθή<SDBG:κριθή:000000>} ‘barley,’ {D:3.44}) pertaining to being made or consisting of barley, a grain somewhat similar to wheat, but regarded as less desirable for food

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: to decide a question of legal right or wrong, and thus determine the innocence or guilt of the accused and assign appropriate punishment or retribution{N:001}
s.g: to decide a legal question; to act as a judge; making a legal decision; to arrive at a verdict; to try a case (in the passive to stand trial)
s.c: The process of legal judging is often expressed idiomatically. In Africa, one of the standard phrases for judging is ‘to cut a palaver,’ but other expressions in other languages may be ‘to find guilt,’ ‘to point the finger at wrong,’ or ‘to untangle strife.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρίνω<SDBG:κρίνω:000004>}[e] ‘to judge legal cases,’ {D:56.20}) the authority or right to judge guilt or innocence
s.g: the right to judge; the authority to judge

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: the legal decision rendered by a judge, whether for or against the accused

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: to judge a person to be guilty and liable to punishment{N:002}
s.g: to judge as guilty; to condemn; condemnation

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Lawsuit, Case
s.d: legal action taken in a court of law against someone{N:003}
s.c: In most languages there are technical terms for lawsuits or cases in court, but where these do not exist, one may always use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘to accuse someone before a judge’ or ‘to argue against someone in court’ or ‘to say in court that someone has done a person harm.’

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρίνω<SDBG:κρίνω:000002>}[c] ‘to judge,’ {D:30.108}) the content of the process of judging

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: any one of several types of flowers, usually uncultivated
s.c: Though traditionally κρίνον has been regarded as a type of lily, scholars have suggested several other possible references, including an anemone, a poppy, a gladiolus, and a rather inconspicuous type of daisy.

s.dp: Think › To Decide, To Conclude
s.d: to come to a conclusion in the process of thinking and thus to be in a position to make a decision{N:001}
s.g: to come to a conclusion; to decide; to make up one’s mind
s.c: In some languages the process of ‘deciding’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to come to the end in one’s thinking’ or ‘to choose in one’s mind’ or ‘the mind sees its goal.’

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to judge something to be better than something else, and hence, to prefer
s.g: to prefer; to judge as superior; to regard as more valuable

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: to make a judgment based upon the correctness or value of something{N:002}

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Have an Opinion, Hold a View
s.d: to hold a view or have an opinion with regard to something
s.g: to hold a view; to have an opinion; to consider; to regard

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: to decide a question of legal right or wrong, and thus determine the innocence or guilt of the accused and assign appropriate punishment or retribution{N:003}
s.g: to decide a legal question; to act as a judge; making a legal decision; to arrive at a verdict; to try a case (in the passive to stand trial)
s.c: The process of legal judging is often expressed idiomatically. In Africa, one of the standard phrases for judging is ‘to cut a palaver,’ but other expressions in other languages may be ‘to find guilt,’ ‘to point the finger at wrong,’ or ‘to untangle strife.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: to judge a person to be guilty and liable to punishment{N:004}
s.g: to judge as guilty; to condemn; condemnation

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: to rule over people
s.c: Though it would be possible to understand κρίνω in ⟦Luke 22:30|Luke 22:30⟧ as meaning ‘to judge’ (see LN 56.30), the function of the twelve disciples seems to be far greater than that. Furthermore, there seems to be a significant Semitic influence in the meaning of κρίνω, since the corresponding Hebrew term likewise involved far more than merely making judicial decisions.

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: act of deciding a question of legal right or wrong, and thus determining the innocence or guilt of the accused and assigning appropriate punishment or retribution{N:001}
s.g: making a legal decision; arriving at a verdict; judgment
s.c: The process of legal judging is often expressed idiomatically. In Africa, one of the standard phrases for judging is ‘to cut a palaver,’ but other expressions in other languages may be ‘to find guilt,’ ‘to point the finger at wrong,’ or ‘to untangle strife.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρίνω<SDBG:κρίνω:000004>}[e] ‘to judge legal cases,’ {D:56.20}) the authority or right to judge guilt or innocence
s.g: the right to judge; the authority to judge

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Court of Justice
s.d: a court of justice for determining guilt or innocence{N:002}
s.c: For languages which do not have technical terms for a court, it is usually possible to use some such phrase as ‘to be brought before a judge’ or ‘to have judges decide one’s case.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: the legal decision rendered by a judge, whether for or against the accused

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: act of judging a person to be guilty and liable to punishment{N:004}

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: the administration of justice
s.c: It may be difficult to speak of ‘justice triumphing,’ and so in some languages it may be necessary to translate ‘so that all accusations are judged justly’ or ‘so that everyone receives what he should’ or ‘until all judgments are just.’

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρίνω<SDBG:κρίνω:000002>}[c] ‘to judge,’ {D:30.108}) the content of the process of judging
s.c: It may also be possible to translate ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνετε (⟦John 7:24|John 7:24⟧) as ‘judge in a righteous manner’ or ‘judge according to true standards.’

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: the basis for rendering a judgment
s.g: basis of judging; basis for judgment
s.c: It is also possible to render κρίσις in ⟦John 3:19|John 3:19⟧ as ‘how judgment works’ or ‘the reason for God judging.’

s.dp: Punish, Reward › Punish
s.d: punishment, with the implication of having been judged guilty
s.c: It is also possible, of course, to interpret κρίσις in ⟦Matthew 23:33|Matthew 23:33⟧ as meaning ‘condemnation’ (see LN 56.30), but as such, punishment is certainly implied.

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to fall under judgment) to be condemned for acting contrary to laws and regulations
s.g: to be condemned; to suffer condemnation; to be judged guilty
s.c: In the context of ⟦James 5:12|James 5:12⟧ the condemnation refers to God’s judgment.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a leader of the synagogue in Corinth

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Court of Justice
s.d: a court of justice for determining guilt or innocence{N:001}
s.c: For languages which do not have technical terms for a court, it is usually possible to use some such phrase as ‘to be brought before a judge’ or ‘to have judges decide one’s case.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Lawsuit, Case
s.d: legal action taken in a court of law against someone{N:002}
s.c: In most languages there are technical terms for lawsuits or cases in court, but where these do not exist, one may always use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘to accuse someone before a judge’ or ‘to argue against someone in court’ or ‘to say in court that someone has done a person harm.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: one who presides over a court session and pronounces judgment

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρίνω<SDBG:κρίνω:000004>}[e] ‘to judge legal cases,’ {D:56.20}) pertaining to the ability or capacity to judge legal cases
s.g: able to judge; to have the capacity to judge

s.dp: Physical Impact › Hit, Strike
s.d: to knock on a door, as a means of signaling one’s presence to those inside
s.c: A literal rendering of κρούω in ⟦Matthew 7:7|Matthew 7:7⟧ may be misleading in a number of languages, since in some areas only thieves knock on doors. This is done in order to determine whether anyone is at home, in which case, of course, the thief runs off. The more general practice for signaling one’s presence may be to cough, to clap the hands, or to call out one’s name.

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: (locative derivative of {L:κρυπτός<SDBG:κρυπτός:000000>} ‘secret, hidden,’ {D:28.69}) a place which is secret or hidden and thus not generally known, possibly referring to a structure built underground for hiding or storing objects{N:001}

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be known, in view of the fact that it has been kept secret
s.g: secret; hidden; not able to be made known
s.c: In a number of languages there may be complications involved in what could be regarded as a triple negation in the sense that ‘nothing,’ ‘secret’ (in the sense of ‘not known’), and ‘not be made known’ are all semantic negations. It may therefore be better to render ⟦Matthew 10:26|Matthew 10:26⟧ as ‘everything that is now not known will be made known.’|In a number of languages ‘secret’ is regularly expressed as ‘not known’ or ‘what is kept from being known.’

s.dp: Psychological Faculties
s.d: (idiom, literally: the hidden (person)) the psychological faculty, including intellectual, emotional, and spiritual aspects, in contrast with the purely physical aspects of human existence
s.g: the inner being; the inmost being; inwardly
s.c: A strictly literal rendering of ἀλλ ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ Ἰουδαῖος might be misunderstood in ⟦Romans 2:29|Romans 2:29⟧ to refer only to the fact of circumcision, which would be something which would normally not be evident.|In a number of languages it is quite impossible to speak of the psychological faculty of a person as being merely ‘that which is within.’ It is frequently necessary to refer to a particular organ of the body, for example, ‘the heart’ or ‘the liver’ or ‘the spleen.’ In some languages, however, one may refer to this faculty as being ‘the person who stands inside’ or ‘the real person’ or even ‘the other person.’|In ⟦Luke 17:21|Luke 17:21⟧ the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν in the statement ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν ‘look, God’s reign is within you’ may constitute a reference to the same inner being designated by the phrases ὁ ἔσω and ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ. On this basis some scholars have suggested that the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν can be interpreted as a potentiality for participation and hence be translated ‘within your grasp,’ but it is more likely that one should understand the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν in ⟦Luke 17:21|Luke 17:21⟧ as a spacial relationship, for example, ‘in your midst’ or ‘among you’ (see LN 83.9).

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: the content of what is not able to be known

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be known by the public but known by some in-group or by those immediately involved
s.g: in secret; in private; secretly; privately

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to being secret as a result of people not knowing

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to cause to be safe or protected by hiding, in some contexts with the intent of not being found
s.g: to keep safe; to cause to be protected; to protect; to hide
s.c: Since κρύπτω also means ‘to make invisible,’ some scholars believe that this statement in ⟦Colossians 3:3|Colossians 3:3⟧ means that ‘your life is concealed in Christ’ or ‘… hidden from view …’ (see LN 24.30). For another interpretation of κρύπτω in ⟦Matthew 13:44|Matthew 13:44⟧, see LN 24.29.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to cause something to be invisible, with the intent of its being not found
s.c: For another interpretation of κρύπτω in ⟦Matthew 13:44|Matthew 13:44⟧, see LN 21.12.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to cause something to be invisible (in the sense of being hidden), but for the purpose of safekeeping and protection
s.g: to hide; to make invisible; to make hidden and safe
s.c: The evident implication of this statement in ⟦Colossians 3:3|Colossians 3:3⟧ is to emphasize the fact that the true life of the believer is not some material, visible object or happening, but something spiritual and thus only visible to those spiritually enlightened or concerned. For another interpretation of κρύπτω in ⟦Colossians 3:3|Colossians 3:3⟧, see LN 21.12.

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: to cause something not to be known{N:001}
s.g: to hide; to keep secret; to conceal
s.c: In a number of languages, the causative relationships involved in ⟦Matthew 11:25|Matthew 11:25⟧ must be made somewhat more explicit, for example, ‘because you have kept the wise and learned people from knowing and have caused the unlearned to know.’ In ⟦Matthew 11:25|Matthew 11:25⟧ νήπιος is used figuratively in reference to unlearned people.

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: (derivative of {L:κρύσταλλος<SDBG:κρύσταλλος:000000>}[a] ‘crystal,’ {D:2.46}) to shine in the same way that crystal shines
s.g: to shine like crystal; to shine brightly

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: a very hard, translucent, and usually transparent type of quartz
s.c: The equivalent of ‘crystal’ is often a descriptive phrase such as ‘a brilliant stone’ or ‘a shining stone’ or ‘a glass-like stone.’ In developing a satisfactory term for crystal, it is important to avoid possible confusion with diamond.|Some scholars, however, interpret κρύσταλλος in ⟦Revelation 4:6|Revelation 4:6⟧ as being a reference to ice (see LN 2.11).

s.dp: Natural Substances › Water
s.d: frozen water
s.c: In both ⟦Revelation 4:6|Revelation 4:6⟧ and ⟦Revelation 22:1|Revelation 22:1⟧ (the only two passages in which κρύσταλλος occurs in the NT) the meaning may, however, be ‘rock crystal’ rather than ‘ice’ (see LN 2.46).|Though in the Arctic regions people may have a number of different terms for various kinds and forms of ice, there are many areas in the world in which there is no existing local term for ‘ice.’ Sometimes a descriptive phrase such as ‘hardened water’ is employed, and in a number of languages a term is simply borrowed from a dominant language of the region. However, in ⟦Revelation 4:6|Revelation 4:6⟧ and ⟦Revelation 22:1|Revelation 22:1⟧ it is possible to focus upon the brilliance of color rather than the particular substance and thus to speak of λαμπρὸς ὡς κρύσταλλος as ‘that which is sparkling white’ or ‘… bright white.’

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be known by the public but known by some in-group or by those immediately involved
s.g: in secret; in private; secretly; privately

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to acquire possession of something{N:001}
s.g: to get; to acquire; to gain

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to acquire one’s soul, or: to acquire one’s life) to save oneself from grave danger or death
s.g: to save oneself; to protect oneself

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sexual Relations
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to possess a vessel) a euphemistic manner of referring to sexual relations
s.c: It is also possible to understand σκεῦος in ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:4|1 Thessalonians 4:4⟧ as one’s wife (see LN 10.55). σκεῦος in ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:4|1 Thessalonians 4:4⟧ may also be understood as one’s body, and therefore the phrase τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι may be rendered as ‘to control his own body’ (see LN 8.6).

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: (derivative of {L:κτάομαι<SDBG:κτάομαι:000000>} ‘to acquire,’ {D:57.58}) that which is owned or possessed (usually land)

s.dp: Animals
s.d: a larger type of domesticated animal, primarily one used for riding or carrying loads
s.g: beast of burden; riding animal; cattle
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 15:39|1 Corinthians 15:39⟧ (ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων ‘another is the flesh of animals, another the flesh of birds, and another the flesh of fish’) one might argue that κτηνῶν is simply a highly generic expression for all kinds of animals, but in view of its meaning in so many other contexts, it probably applies even in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:39|1 Corinthians 15:39⟧ to large domesticated animals.|As in so many instances, the translator must render passages in terms of expressions which are appropriate to particular contexts. For example, in ⟦Acts 23:24|Acts 23:24⟧ a translation such as ‘horses’ would be appropriate, while in ⟦Luke 10:34|Luke 10:34⟧ the term ‘donkey’ would be fitting, and in ⟦Revelation 18:13|Revelation 18:13⟧ κτήνη (in which κτῆνος contrasts with πρόβατα ‘sheep’) would perhaps best be translated as ‘cattle.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: (derivative of {L:κτάομαι<SDBG:κτάομαι:000000>} ‘to acquire,’ {D:57.58}) one who owns or possesses property

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: to make or create something which has not existed before
s.g: to create; creation (in the NT, used exclusively of God’s activity in creation)

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: act of making or creating something which has not existed before
s.g: creation (in the NT, used exclusively of God’s activity in creation)

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: that which has been created
s.g: creation; creature; what has been created

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Universe, Creation
s.d: the universe as the product of God’s activity in creation
s.c: The meaning of κτίσις might very well be treated as a simple derivative of the verb κτίζω ‘to create’ (LN 42.35), since the reference is to the result of God’s creative act. However, in a number of contexts, the process of creation is no longer focal, and what is in focus is the total physical universe. In some languages the meaning may be best expressed as ‘the world and all that is in it’ or even ‘everything that exists.’

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: (derivative of {L:κτίζω<SDBG:κτίζω:000000>} ‘to create,’ {D:42.35}) a human institution or social structure as something which has been created
s.c: It is possible that κτίσις in ⟦1 Peter 2:13|1 Peter 2:13⟧ may have the implication of authorized institution. It might even be possible to render κτίσις in such a context as ‘authority’ (compare κτίσις in LN 37.43).

s.dp: Control, Rule › Exercise Authority
s.d: an instituted authority, with the implication that such an authority has been created or formed
s.c: The expression ‘human authority’ may be rendered as ‘every person who has the right to rule.’ For another interpretation of κτίσις in ⟦1 Peter 2:13|1 Peter 2:13⟧, see LN 42.39.

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: that which has been created
s.g: creation; creature; what has been created

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: (derivative of {L:κτίζω<SDBG:κτίζω:000000>} ‘to create,’ {D:42.35}) one who creates

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mislead, Lead Astray, Deceive
s.d: trickery that results from craftiness (κυβεία literally refers to dice playing)

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Guide, Lead
s.d: (derivative of κυβερνάω ‘to steer a ship, to guide,’ not occurring in the NT) the ability to lead
s.c: ‘The gift of leadership’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘being able to lead others’ or ‘being able to get others to follow.’

s.dp: Maritime Activities
s.d: one who commands a ship
s.c: In some languages a captain is simply ‘the chief of a ship’ or ‘one who commands the sailors.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Go Around, Surround
s.d: to move in such a way as to encircle an object{N:001}

s.dp: Linear Movement › Go Around, Surround
s.d: to move around an object
s.c: A strictly literal translation of the Greek text of ⟦Hebrews 11:30|Hebrews 11:30⟧ may be extremely difficult, since it is usually necessary to employ an active form involving movement so as to specify what entities go around. Therefore, it may be preferable to translate ‘the walls of Jericho fell after the Israelites had gone around them for seven days.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Go Around, Surround
s.d: to move in such a way as to encircle an object{N:001}

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Around, About, Outside
s.d: a position completely encircling an area or object

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Around, About, Outside
s.d: a position on the total outside surface of a three-dimensional object

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Around, About, Outside
s.d: a position completely encircling an area or object

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: the motion of an object rolling back and forth or rolling about{N:001}
s.c: It is rare that one can use in a language the same or related terms for the rolling of a person in an epileptic fit and the wallowing of a pig in the mud. The first is chaotic and uncontrolled, while the second is both purposeful and slower.

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: the motion of an object rolling back and forth or rolling about{N:001}
s.c: It is rare that one can use in a language the same or related terms for the rolling of a person in an epileptic fit and the wallowing of a pig in the mud. The first is chaotic and uncontrolled, while the second is both purposeful and slower.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: pertaining to a disability in one or more limbs, especially the leg or foot, often as the result of some deformity

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: a moving ridge or succession of swells on the surface of a body of water

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: a percussion instrument consisting of two metal discs which were struck together in order to make a shrill, clashing sound
s.c: The equivalent of κύμβαλον is in many instances a phrase such as ‘loud metal.’

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: probably the plant Cuminum cyminum; same family as carrot; branches from the base and has similar leaves and flowers, though seeds have a sharper smell; planted and harvested each year, reaching a height of about 50-60 cm; seeds are used in cooking and as medicine
s.c: In designating ‘cumin’ as well as ἄνηθον ‘dill,’ πήγανον ‘rue,’ and ἡδύοσμον ‘mint,’ it is probably wise to borrow a term and use a classifier, for example, ‘a seasoning herb called cumin.’

s.dp: Animals
s.d: relatively small light brown domestic animal, feeding on anything from household refuse to animal carcasses and excreta; Canis familiaris putiatini; associated with all sorts of uncleanness, aggression, greediness, low status (diminutive of {L:κύων<SDBG:κύων:000000>}[a] dog, {D:4.34}, but in the NT the diminutive force may have become lost, though a component of emotive attachment or affection is no doubt retained and thus the reference is presumably to a house dog)

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Κύπρος<SDBG:Κύπρος:000000>} ‘Cyprus,’ {D:93.510}) a person who is a native of Cyprus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island off the south coast of Asia Minor

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Κυρήνη<SDBG:Κυρήνη:000000>} ‘Cyrene,’ {D:93.512}) a person who lives in or is a native of Cyrene

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the coast of north Africa

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the imperial governor of Syria

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a title of respect used in addressing or speaking of a woman
s.c: It is likely, however, that κυρία in ⟦2 John 1:1|2 John 1:1⟧ refers to the church as a lady.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (derivative of {L:κύριος<SDBG:κύριος:000000>}[a] ‘Lord,’ {D:12.9}) pertaining to the Lord
s.c: A strictly literal rendering of ‘the Lord’s Supper’ might simply mean ‘the supper which the Lord ate,’ implying that no one else participated. Therefore, it may be necessary in some languages to translate ‘the meal at which the Lord presided’ or ‘the meal which the Lord had for his disciples’ or ‘the meal which the Lord ate with his followers.’

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: to rule or reign over, with the implication in some contexts of lording it over{N:001}
s.g: to rule; to govern; to reign over

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for God and for Christ) one who exercises supernatural authority over mankind (see also {D:37.51})
s.c: The most common equivalent of ‘Lord’ is a term meaning ‘chief’ or ‘leader,’ but frequently this cannot be employed as a title for ‘God.’ One may, however, combine such an expression with a term for ‘God’ and employ a phrase meaning ‘God our leader’ or ‘God our chief.’ In some instances, however, a term for ‘Lord’ is related to a verb meaning ‘to command’ or ‘to order,’ and therefore ‘Lord’ is rendered as ‘the one who commands us’ and combined with ‘God’ may form a phrase such as ‘God, the one who commands us.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: one who owns and controls property, including especially servants and slaves, with important supplementary semantic components of high status and respect

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: one who rules or exercises authority over others
s.c: For the meaning of κύριος as a title for God or for Christ, see LN 12.9.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a title of respect used in addressing or speaking of a man

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to his own master he stands or falls, probably a familiar adage) whether one maintains one’s status or relationship to a master depends on the master's judgment or evaluation
s.g: honor or disgrace depends on the person whom one serves

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: (derivative of {L:κύριος<SDBG:κύριος:000002>}[c] ‘one who rules,’ {D:37.51}) a supernatural ruling power
s.c: In general, the series of terms θρόνοι, κυριότητες, ἀρχαί, and ἐξουσίαι in ⟦Colossians 1:16|Colossians 1:16⟧ (as well as in ⟦Ephesians 1:21|Ephesians 1:21⟧) are understood as being supernatural cosmic powers, whether angelic or demonic (see LN 12.44), but it is possible that these should be understood in terms of human rulers.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: (title for supernatural forces and powers) a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
s.g: power; authority; lordship; ruler; wicked force
s.c: Some scholars have believed that it is possible to reconstruct at least in part some of the hierarchy represented by these various supernatural forces and powers, on the basis of the neoplatonic system of nine such powers arranged in three orders of three each. NT terminology and usage does not, however, lend itself to such a classification, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to determine what are the significant differences between these supernatural powers and forces.|In the case of ⟦Ephesians 1:21|Ephesians 1:21⟧ some scholars apply the terms in question both to the supernatural and to the human sphere, thus emphasizing the totality of Christ’s rule. This has a considerable measure of justification in view of the concepts held by persons in the ancient world, since various earthly powers were supposed to reflect corresponding supernatural powers.|For the most part, translators have endeavored to render the various terms in somewhat different ways, for example, ἐξουσία as ‘authority’; δύναμις as ‘power’; κυριότης as ‘ruler’; and phrases such as τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις as ‘wicked spiritual forces in the heavenly world.’ In a number of languages, however, there are simply not enough terms to designate various kinds of powers, authorities, and forces which could be employed in speaking of such supernatural impersonal powers. Accordingly, some translators have simply used a phrase such as ‘any and all kinds of supernatural powers.’ Where it is possible to make certain lexical distinctions between terms and phrases, this, of course, should be done, but in a number of contexts this may be impossible, and accordingly, some explanation in a marginal note may be required if the reader is to understand satisfactorily the intent of the passages in question.

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: to invest something with power or force
s.g: to give force to; to validate
s.c: In order to express the meaning of this phrase in ⟦Galatians 3:15|Galatians 3:15⟧, it may be necessary in some languages to make more specific the arrangements involved, for example, ‘if people have signed an agreement, no one can disregard it’ or ‘if an agreement has been confirmed, no one can say it does not exist’ or, as in some languages, ‘if an agreement has been tied, no one can untie it.’

s.dp: Real, Unreal
s.d: to cause someone to recognize the reality of something
s.g: to show something to be real; to make something real

s.dp: Animals
s.d: relatively small light brown domestic animal, feeding on anything from household refuse to animal carcasses and excreta; Canis familiaris putiatini; associated with all sorts of uncleanness, aggression, greediness, low status
s.c: In Greek outside the NT κύων may be either masculine or feminine and in the plural may refer to both male and female dogs.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κύων<SDBG:κύων:000000>}[a] ‘dog,’ {D:4.34}) a particularly bad person, perhaps specifically one who ridicules what is holy
s.c: It is also possible that κύων in ⟦Philippians 3:2|Philippians 3:2⟧ may be interpreted as meaning ‘pervert’ (see LN 88.282).|A term for ‘dog’ may have quite a different connotation than it does in English. For example, to call a person ‘a dog’ in some languages is to compliment him for his faithfulness, but in other languages it may be merely a way of attributing promiscuous sexual behavior.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sexual Misbehavior
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κύων<SDBG:κύων:000000>}[a] ‘dog,’ {D:4.34}) one who is a sexual pervert or possibly one who is sexually promiscuous
s.c: It is also possible, however, that in ⟦Revelation 22:15|Revelation 22:15⟧ κύων means ‘a wicked person’ who might have complete contempt for what is holy, a meaning which parallels the significance of the adage in ⟦Matthew 7:6|Matthew 7:6⟧ (see LN 88.122).

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: the dead body of a person, especially one which is still unburied{N:001}
s.c: Though in ⟦Hebrews 3:17|Hebrews 3:17⟧ the Greek text reads literally ‘whose dead bodies fell in the wilderness,’ it would normally be a mistake to translate this clause literally, since it might suggest that the people died while they were still standing, and that only the corpses fell. A more natural equivalent is ‘they died in the wilderness’ or ‘they died and their bodies lay in the wilderness.’

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to cause something not to happen{N:001}

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Population Centers
s.d: a relatively unimportant population center (in contrast with {L:πόλις<SDBG:πόλις:000001>}[b] ‘city,’ {D:1.89})

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: the inhabitants of a village{N:001}
s.g: the people there; the people of a village
s.c: Though in English it may seem perfectly appropriate to speak of ‘announcing the good news to a town’ or ‘… a village,’ in a number of languages this is simply not possible, for any announcement of good news must be directed to people and not to a place or area.

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Population Centers
s.d: a city that had the status of a {L:κώμη<SDBG:κώμη:000000>} ({D:1.92}) as far as its legal standing or constitution was concerned

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: drinking parties involving unrestrained indulgence in alcoholic beverages and accompanying immoral behavior

s.dp: Animals › Insects
s.d: small flying insect; feeds on human or animal blood; regarded as pest
s.c: The straining of liquids referred to in ⟦Matthew 23:24|Matthew 23:24⟧ is based on the regulations in Leviticus 11, in which the gnat is the smallest of the unclean creatures and the camel the largest.|For the only occurrence of κώνωψ in the NT, one may use a term which refers to any small flying insect which might fall into a beverage and thus have to be strained out.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island in the Aegean Sea

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: pertaining to not being able to speak or talk
s.g: dumb; mute; unable to speak; incapable of talking

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Hear
s.d: pertaining to being unable to hear
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘deaf’ is an idiom, for example, ‘his ears are closed’ or ‘he has no ears’ or ‘his ears are stone.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Receive
s.d: to receive, with the implication that the process is related somehow to divine will or favor
s.c: It is, however, possible to interpret λαγχάνω in ⟦Acts 1:17|Acts 1:17⟧ and in ⟦2 Peter 1:1|2 Peter 1:1⟧ as referring to the process of divine choice and thus translate as ‘be chosen to have.’

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to choose by lot, probably by the use of marked pebbles or pieces of pottery
s.g: to choose by lot; to decide by gambling
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent to ‘casting lots,’ particularly for this type of context, is ‘to gamble.’

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to be selected by a decision based on the casting of lots, with the possible implication of reflecting divine choice
s.g: to be chosen by lot; to be selected by lot

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the brother of {L:Mary<SDBG:Μαρία:000001>}[b] and {L:Marta<SDBG:Μάρθα:000000>}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a beggar in a parable

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be known by the public but known by some in-group or by those immediately involved
s.g: in secret; in private; secretly; privately

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Wind
s.d: sudden and violent gusts of winds, often from varied directions{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages a strong wind which causes the waves or a storm on water must be referred to by a special term. Compare, for example, the English term squall; this would mean a wind of relatively short duration but sufficiently intense so as to create relatively high waves.

s.dp: Physical Impact › Split, Tear
s.d: to burst open, probably from internal pressure

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Resistance
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to kick against the goad) to react against authority in such a way as to cause harm or suffering to oneself
s.g: to hurt oneself by reacting against a person or command

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: to speak or talk, with the possible implication of more informal usage (though this cannot be clearly and consistently shown from NT contexts)
s.g: to speak; to say; to talk; to tell

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to speak to the ear) to speak quietly and presumably to a restricted audience
s.c: For another treatment of the phrase πρὸς τὸ οὖς, see LN 28.73.

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: (derivative of λαλέω ‘to speak,’ 33.70) that which has been spoken or uttered

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: a particular manner of speech

s.dp: Relations › Cause and/or Reason
s.d: an (Aramaic) interrogative expression of reason

s.dp: Attachment › Grasp, Hold
s.d: to take hold of something or someone, with or without force
s.g: to take hold of; to grasp; to grab
s.c: A number of languages differ radically in terms for ‘taking hold of,’ depending upon whether force is employed, whether the object is a thing or an animate being, and whether the language incorporates into a verb of ‘taking hold of’ a classification as to the objects involved, for example, long and thin, round and flat, ball-like, angular, or lumpy.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to acquire possession of something{N:001}
s.g: to take; to acquire; to obtain
s.c: In some languages ‘take’ in ⟦Matthew 5:40|Matthew 5:40⟧ may be best rendered as ‘go away with’ or ‘put it on as his own.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Receive
s.d: to receive or accept an object or benefit for which the initiative rests with the giver, but the focus of attention in the transfer is upon the receiver{N:002}

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to collect what is due (normally in terms of taxes and interest), with the possible implication of extortion (as in {S:04200301300024})

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to make a choice of one or more possible alternatives
s.g: to choose; to select; to prefer
s.c: In a number of languages the choice of terms or expressions for ‘choosing’ or ‘selecting’ often depends upon either (1) what is chosen or selected or (2) the purpose for such a choice, for example, personal pleasure, rational evaluation, or outright prejudice.|It is also possible to interpret λαμβάνω in ⟦Hebrews 5:1|Hebrews 5:1⟧ as meaning ‘to acquire, to obtain’ (see λαμβάνω, LN 57.55).

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to come to believe something and to act in accordance with such a belief
s.g: to accept; to receive; to come to believe

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Exploit
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:λαμβάνω<SDBG:λαμβάνω:000000>}[a] ‘to take hold,’ {D:18.1}) to take advantage of someone by trickery or deception
s.g: to exploit by deception; to take advantage of by trickery

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to experience some event or state, often with the implication of something negatively valued{N:003}

s.dp: Case › To Cause To Experience
s.d: to cause to experience, normally implying something grievous
s.c: It is, of course, possible to understand λαμβάνω in ⟦Mark 14:65|Mark 14:65⟧ in a more or less literal sense (see LN 18.1) and thus to translate this expression as ‘the guards took him and slapped him.’

s.dp: Activities Involving Clothing and Adorning
s.d: to put on an article of clothing

s.dp: Case › Agent of a Numerable Event
s.d: a marker of an agent relation with numerable events, with the implication of having assumed some initiative

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take a rule, to receive a rule) to receive from someone else the power or authority to reign as a king

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Courage, Boldness
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take courage) to become confident or courageous in the face of real or possible danger
s.g: to become confident; to take courage

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take face) to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
s.g: to show favoritism; to be partial; partiality
s.c: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: (a productive idiomatic expression, literally: to take one’s cross) to be prepared to endure severe suffering, even to the point of death
s.g: to be prepared to suffer even unto death; to take up one’s cross
s.c: The idiom ‘to carry one’s cross’ or ‘to take up one’s cross’ involves a number of important features of meaning. Unfortunately, this expression is frequently not understood correctly by many people who hear it or even use it. One reason for this is the actual absence of crucifixion in modern society. If a literal translation is to be employed, then some marginal note will probably be necessary in order to indicate clearly the full implications of such a statement.

s.dp: Aspect › Try, Attempt
s.d: to attempt to do something, with the implication of not succeeding{N:006}
s.c: In a number of languages expressions such as πειράζω, πειράομαι, and πεῖραν λαμβάνω may be expressed as to start to do something, but not be able to or to think that one can do something, but discover it is impossible.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Noah in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Artifacts › Lights and Light Holders
s.d: a stick or bundle of sticks carried about as a light

s.dp: Artifacts › Lights and Light Holders
s.d: a light made by burning a wick saturated with oil contained in a relatively small vessel
s.c: In some languages the closest equivalent of λαμπάς and λύχνος is a kerosene lamp. What is to be avoided is a word which suggests a flashlight, which would of course be highly anachronistic.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: pertaining to being bright or shining, either of a source or of an object which is illuminated by a source

s.dp: Features of Objects › Transparent
s.d: pertaining to being clear and also bright

s.dp: Features of Objects › Glorious
s.d: pertaining to being brilliant or splendid, though with the possible implication of ostentatious or superficial
s.c: See note at LN 79.21.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: the state of brightness or shining
s.c: In a number of languages a clear distinction is made between some object which is bright in and of itself (that is to say, the source of brightness or radiance) and objects which are bright because they reflect light from some source. In the case of ⟦Matthew 17:5|Matthew 17:5⟧ (which is generally regarded as a reference to the Shekinah presence of God), the cloud would not be merely reflecting light but would be a source of light (see LN 14.50).

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Extravagant Living, Intemperate Living
s.d: pertaining to living in ostentatious luxury
s.c: The equivalent of λαμπρῶς in the sense of ‘luxuriously’ may be rendered in a number of languages as ‘richly’ or ‘with things which cost a great deal’ or ‘with more possessions than one can count.’

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: to shine or to produce light, as in the case of heavenly bodies, lightning, candles, torches, etc.
s.g: to shine; to give light; to bring light
s.c: Terms for ‘shining, giving light’ often differ depending upon the type of source. There may be, for example, a contrast between the shining of a heavenly body in contrast with some source on earth. There may also be a difference between a continuous shining such as of the sun and the moon and a brief flash, as in the case of lightning or sparks from a fire.

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: to cause oneself to not be known, with the implication of concealment and secrecy
s.g: to escape notice; to remain hidden
s.c: In some languages this expression in ⟦Mark 7:24|Mark 7:24⟧ may be rendered as ‘he was not able to keep people from knowing where he was’ or ‘he was not able to keep secret where he was.’

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Not Remembering, Forgetting
s.d: to not recall information and thus to lose sight of its significance
s.g: to forget; to not remember; to lose sight of; to ignore
s.c: In a number of languages the fact of ‘forgetting’ or ‘not remembering’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to lose out of one’s heart,’ ‘to have one’s thoughts walk away,’ or ‘to have words disappear from one’s liver.’

s.dp: Know
s.d: to not have knowledge about or to be unaware of something, with the implication that something can readily escape notice or be hidden
s.g: to be unaware of; to not know

s.dp: Physical Impact › Pierce, Cut
s.d: pertaining to having been hewn out of rock
s.c: In ⟦Luke 23:53|Luke 23:53⟧ ‘rock’ must be understood as a basic outcropping of rock, so that the grave would have been a cave-like structure cut into a rock outcropping.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Phrygia in Asia Minor

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Λαοδίκεια<SDBG:Λαοδίκεια:000000>} ‘Laodicea,’ {D:93.514}) a person who lives in or is a native of Laodicea

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: the largest unit into which the people of the world are divided on the basis of their constituting a socio-political community
s.c: In a number of languages a term meaning basically ‘tribe’ has been extended in meaning to identify ‘nations.’ In other instances different nations are spoken of simply as ‘different peoples.’ In certain cases distinct nations are classified primarily in terms of their diverse languages, for example, ‘those people who speak different languages.’ Such an expression should not, however, be used if it only refers to multilingual persons.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a collective for people who belong to God (whether Jews or Christians)
s.c: The phrase ‘people of God’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘the people who belong to God’ or ‘the people whom God possesses,’ but in a number of languages the relationship between the people and God must be expressed in terms of reverence or worship, for example, ‘the people who worship God’ or ‘the people who reverence God.’ See also LN 11.27.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: a casual non-membership group of people, fairly large in size and assembled for whatever purpose{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages there is no term corresponding to ‘crowd.’ One may, however, usually speak of such a group of people as ‘many people’ or ‘many men and women.’ Depending on the context, it may be necessary to indicate some relative difference in size, for example, ‘very large crowd’ or ‘many, many people.’ If the crowd is relatively small, one may sometimes speak of ‘just some people.’

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: the common people, in contrast with those who are rich, leaders, and/or authorities in the society, often with the implication of disdain and low esteem
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘the common people’ is ‘the poor people,’ but in some languages an equivalent depends upon geographical location, for example, ‘those who live on the edge of town’ (the opposite situation from what exists in most present-day metropolitan centers). In still other languages ‘the common people’ may be designated in terms of lack of status, for example, ‘those who have no position’ or ‘those whom the rich do not greet’ or ‘those before whom no one ever bows.’

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.c: The context of ⟦Romans 3:13|Romans 3:13⟧ is highly figurative, and in a number of languages it may be necessary either to change the metaphor into a simile, for example, ‘their throat is like an open tomb,’ or to employ a somewhat altered equivalent, for example, ‘their speech is full of deadly deceit.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the south coast of the island of Crete

s.dp: Physical Impact › Pierce, Cut
s.d: to shape rock by cutting, either internally or externally
s.g: to cut rock; to hew out rock
s.c: In some languages important distinctions are made in terms for cutting rock depending upon the type of activity, for example, shaping of rock by cutting, the quarrying of rock from an outcrop, or the hewing of an area inside of an outcropping of rock (a cave-like structure hewn into rock).

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: to perform religious rites as a part of worship{N:001}
s.g: to perform religious rites; to worship; to venerate; worship
